aidb_assessment.novelty: The central novelty is not memory accumulation itself but an observability-driven repair interface that connects failures to local regions of executable memory-provider code, preserves compatible runtime memory, records repair outcomes, and permits an explicit no-patch decision. This is a meaningful distinction from methods that revise only memory content or generate complete replacement architectures.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The evidence supports careful reading and replication rather than immediate adoption. Results are consistent across information-seeking and embodied tasks, and the paper reports consequential negative evidence instead of only aggregate gains. Confidence remains moderate because the comparisons are mostly point estimates, some trajectories confound code and memory changes, the patch-history component underperforms the simpler evidence condition in the diagnostic ablation, and the supplied material lacks executable artifacts.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High potential usefulness for agent systems with editable memory providers: the framework offers a concrete diagnosis workflow, guards against broad rewrites, surfaces regressions, and provides interpretable patch manifests. The strongest practical signal is the controlled diagnostic ablation plus matched-start evaluations. Adoption should wait for independent replication, multi-run stability, stronger safety checks, and tests across additional starting architectures.

executive_summary: MemScope treats memory-architecture evolution as evidence-grounded repair of an existing provider. A Patch Agent inspects traces, stored memory, retrieval behavior, and code, then makes bounded replacements while retaining compatible memory. A controlled GAIA diagnostic favors trace-and-memory inspection over summary-only or trace-only feedback; matched-start tests also favor the evolved provider on xBench and unseen ALFWorld tasks. The method explicitly allows no-patch decisions and tracks regressions. Evidence remains limited by narrow executors and backbones, one starting architecture, single reported trajectories, and online comparisons where code and memory both change. Small edit counts do not guarantee small behavioral effects. The supplied document describes prompts and checks but does not identify executable artifacts sufficient for independent reproduction.

assumptions: Segment accuracy on a task window is an adequate signal for deciding when provider repair should be attempted.
Probe evidence and the available skill descriptions are sufficient for routing to a suitable memory skill or deciding that global exploration is needed.
Raw traces, stored memory, retrieval decisions, and provider code contain enough information to localize a consequential failure.
The frozen executor isolates provider evolution sufficiently, although online memory contents continue changing.
Local syntactic and interface checks are useful proxies for safe installation; behavioral regressions are detected later through continued execution.
Retaining runtime memory across a patch is valid when compatibility constraints pass.
GPT-4o-mini judgments adequately represent correctness for GAIA and xBench, while ALFWorld environment success is an adequate outcome measure.
key_components: A memory skill separates natural-language guidance in SKILL.md, executable memory_retrieval and memory_storage methods, and a skill-specific runtime memory bank.
The Memory Skill Router selects among human-designed skills using probe executions; a Skill Designer and full provider generation form a global-exploration fallback.
The Agent Executor is frozen during provider evolution and records answers, raw trajectories, distilled memory items, accuracy, time, and cost.
The repair trigger uses degradation relative to historical best performance plus a minimum failure count to decide whether diagnosis should run.
Trace tools expose cases, headers, native steps, and cross-trace events; memory tools expose record statistics, raw records, queries, matches, selection decisions, and retrieval output.
The Patch Agent grounds a proposed repair in traces, runtime memory, provider code, skill intent, and optional history, then produces localized replacements and a risk manifest.
Patch History records proposals, installation decisions, recovered failures, and regressed successes so later repairs can revise an unsuccessful direction.
Local validation protects provider identity, schema compatibility, required interfaces, imports, and isolated retrieval; the system can retain the current provider through no_patch.
method.overview: An episode begins with probe tasks and selection of an existing memory skill; global provider generation is available only when no skill is suitable. A frozen Agent Executor processes sequential task segments using provider-controlled retrieval and storage against a separate runtime memory bank. A trigger compares current segment accuracy with the best previous episode on the same task window and invokes a tool-using Patch Agent after a sufficient decline and at least one failure. The Patch Agent performs read-only inspection of successful and failed traces, raw memory records, retrieval matches and decisions, the current provider, the skill specification, and patch history. It emits exact old-to-new replacements plus a manifest describing root cause, expected effect, and risk. Local checks enforce syntax, identity, memory compatibility, required methods, and in later experiments import and isolated-retrieval behavior. Valid patches are installed in place while the runtime bank is retained; insufficient evidence may produce a no-patch decision.

open_questions: Does MemScope retain its advantage when original and evolved providers are evaluated with frozen, identical memory banks?
How often does the trigger fire, and what fractions of invocations yield installed patches, rejected patches, failed checks, or no-patch decisions?
What are the distributions of gains and regressions across repeated runs, task orders, backbones, and starting providers?
Does Patch History improve long-run cumulative performance despite its lower diagnostic-ablation score?
How does localized repair compare with complete provider generation under equal task, token, wall-clock, and monetary budgets?
What safety mechanism prevents locally valid patches from producing delayed cross-task regressions or corrupting future memory?
How accurate and stable is GPT-4o-mini as both a correctness evaluator and an indirect source of online feedback?
Are all archived transitions reported, including unsuccessful and reverted edits, or is the locality analysis a selected subset?

problem.importance: Long-horizon agents combine memory contents, retrieval decisions, tool use, and downstream actions. Without localized evidence, an observed failure cannot be reliably mapped to code, so architecture evolution may modify a capable component unnecessarily, propagate regressions, or fail to correct the actual cause.
problem.scope: The paper studies in-place evolution of executable memory-provider code, starting primarily from DynamicCheatsheet and evaluating information-seeking tasks on GAIA and xBench plus sequential household interaction on ALFWorld. It does not establish generality across arbitrary memory architectures, executors, model families, production workloads, or long-term deployment conditions.
problem.statement: Memory architectures usually remain fixed after deployment, while existing self-evolution methods often use aggregate scores or compressed summaries that do not identify which storage, retrieval, presentation, or downstream execution component caused a failure. This leaves architecture updates weakly constrained and can induce broad rewrites when a local correction—or no provider change—would be more appropriate.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Original and evolved providers evaluated on exactly the same frozen memory-bank snapshots, task order, executor, model outputs where replay is possible, and retrieval requests; also include a code-shuffled placebo patch with comparable edit size.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Localized provider repair improves outcomes independently of changes in accumulated runtime memory.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired difference in task correctness, accompanied by recovered-failure and regressed-success counts and a paired confidence interval across tasks and repeated runs.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop and reject code-level attribution if the confidence interval includes no improvement, if gains disappear with frozen memory, or if regressions equal or exceed recoveries in most runs.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Trace + Memory Inspection without history, compared with full history, outcome-only history, and a relevance-filtered history, using identical initial providers, memories, task streams, trigger events, and model budgets.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Patch History improves cumulative evolution performance when enough prior repairs exist, even if it does not improve a short diagnostic ablation.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Area under the online accuracy curve across episodes, with secondary measurements of installed-patch precision, cumulative regressions, no-patch calibration, and diagnosis cost.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop adding history if it fails to improve the primary metric across multiple independent task orders or increases cumulative regressions or diagnosis cost beyond a preregistered tolerance.

proposed_experiments.baseline: MemScope versus full-provider generation and no-evolution controls, budget-matched for executor calls, diagnostic tokens, patch-generation tokens, validation tasks, wall time, and monetary cost across several structurally distinct memory architectures.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Localized repair offers a better accuracy–cost–risk trade-off than complete architecture regeneration across diverse starting memory providers.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Mean held-out task gain per unit total evolution cost, jointly reported with worst-case regression rate and semantic edit-impact measures.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop claiming a general trade-off advantage if MemScope loses on the primary metric for most starting architectures, if its worst-case regression rate exceeds the full-generation baseline, or if gains depend only on DynamicCheatsheet.

It supports raw trace access and an inspectable memory store, but not the incremental value of patch history.
